# Set up Thermite: instructions for an AI agent

You are an AI agent helping a person set up Thermite on their computer. Thermite is open-source
autoresearch: AI agents run experiments on a project in a loop, and a judge the agents cannot
see or change keeps only what it measures as better. Its documentation is https://usethermite.com.

Follow these steps in order. Run the commands yourself where you can, say what each one does
before you run it, and stop to ask the person when a step needs their choice or their hands.

## Rules while you work

- Never read, print, copy or paste a token, key or password: not into this chat, not into a
  file, not into a command line. Where a step needs one, tell the person the command that shows
  it, and let them copy it themselves.
- Never publish Thermite's ports to the internet. Its dashboard stays at 127.0.0.1:8800. To
  reach it from other machines, use a private network (step 6).
- Thermite's agents run code that an AI model writes, on this computer. Before the person gives
  Thermite a model, have them read Known limits: https://usethermite.com/reference/known-limits/
  and, before they use a paid key, set a budget:
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/campaigns/budget-and-stop-time/
- Use the latest release, as below. Don't build Thermite from source unless the person asks:
  that is for contributors.

## 1. Check what the computer has

Thermite needs:

- Linux or macOS, with a few CPU cores, a few gigabytes of free memory, and several gigabytes of
  free disk (its images take about 2.5 GB).
- Docker with Docker Compose 2 or later (`docker compose version`), or Podman with
  `podman compose` (`podman compose version`) and a compose program behind it: podman-compose
  (`pipx install podman-compose`) or Docker Compose 2. Not `docker-compose` 1.x: it can't read
  Thermite's compose file. On a Mac with Podman, its virtual machine must be running
  (`podman machine start`), and the free disk must be inside it.
- curl, and an internet connection.

If something is missing, tell the person what, and how to install it for their system, and ask
before you install anything.

Below, write `docker compose` for Docker, or `podman compose` for Podman.

## 2. Get Thermite

```sh
mkdir thermite
cd thermite
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/releases/latest/download/compose.yaml
```

Check the file: the notes of https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/releases/latest give its
SHA-256 and the command that checks it, which prints `compose.yaml: OK`. If it prints `FAILED`,
download it again; don't use it.

## 3. Make the local tokens

```sh
docker compose run --rm init
```

Its last line is `local init: .dev ready (… made, … kept)`. The tokens are in `.dev/secrets/`.
Don't open them.

## 4. Start Thermite

```sh
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
```

The first start downloads the images, which can take a few minutes. `ps` lists four containers
whose status starts with `Up`: control, nats, harness and supervisor. `init` and `enroll` may
show `Exited (0)`: that is right. Then check control:

```sh
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8800/v1/health
```

It answers `{"ok":true,"bus":"connected","degraded":false}`. A container that isn't Up: read its
log (`docker compose logs <name>`), then
https://usethermite.com/how-to/operate/troubleshoot/

## 5. Have the person sign in

Tell the person to run this themselves and copy what it shows, their owner's token:

```sh
cat .dev/secrets/control-admin-token
```

Then to open http://127.0.0.1:8800/ui, paste it into **Admin token** and press **Sign in**. The
Overview says `1 of 1 rigs reporting` once the rig has reported, within a minute.

The tutorial these steps come from, with what each screen shows:
https://usethermite.com/tutorials/first-run/

## 6. Next, by what the person wants

Ask what they want to do next, and take them to the page for it. Every page is also published as
Markdown at its address with `.md` added, which is easier for you to read.

- Run a first campaign, with a free model and no account:
  https://usethermite.com/tutorials/agents-with-a-free-model/
- Add a second machine: https://usethermite.com/tutorials/second-machine/
- Reach Thermite from other devices or machines, privately, with Tailscale or WireGuard:
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/install/private-network/
- Use this computer's NVIDIA GPUs:
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/install/one-machine/#use-the-machines-nvidia-gpus
- Work on the person's own project: https://usethermite.com/tutorials/your-own-project/
- A campaign that ends when a goal is met: https://usethermite.com/tutorials/first-goal-campaign/
- Choose between a hill climb, a goal campaign and a research campaign:
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/campaigns/choose-a-mode/
- Give the agents a model, free or paid, or a Claude or ChatGPT subscription:
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/models/choose-a-model/
- Rigs elsewhere: on a Kubernetes cluster
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/install/rig-on-a-cluster/ , or a GPU on RunPod
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/install/runpod-rig/
- Let an AI agent (such as you) run campaigns through Thermite's MCP server:
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/automate/agent-over-mcp/
- Keep Thermite running for real work: its settings, ports, updates and backups:
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/install/one-machine/ and
  https://usethermite.com/how-to/operate/backup-and-restore/
- Something went wrong: https://usethermite.com/how-to/operate/troubleshoot/

Every page, listed with what it covers: https://usethermite.com/llms.txt . All of them in one
file: https://usethermite.com/llms-full.txt . What changed in each release:
https://usethermite.com/project/changelog/
